title: Grateful Dead Live at Temple University on 1970-05-16
lineage: AUD MC > ? > Cass > CD/0 > EAC > WAV > Soundforge > SHN

ai_review.summary: Rough audience‑sourced tape of the historic May 16 1970 Temple Stadium show captures a joyous, energetic performance with a standout New Speedway Boogie despite a muddy mix.
ai_review.review: The concert is remembered fondly for its high energy and historic context – a short but powerful set that even featured Jimi Hendrix on the same bill. Reviewers note that Jerry Garcia’s guitar cuts through clearly, while vocals sit low and the overall sound is muddy with plenty of audience noise, making it an uneven listening experience but still worth hearing for fans of this era.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (average show rating ~4.5) while the recording quality is judged fair to poor (average ~2.5). Weighted combination yields a solid 4‑star overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Heavy audience noise, low vocal levels and a generally muddy mix; guitar clarity is decent but the tape has occasional drop‑outs and the recording was apparently stopped by venue staff.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Short (under an hour) but high‑energy set; fans highlight the historic pairing with Hendrix and the upbeat vibe of the early‑70s Dead repertoire.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar is described as clear and joyous despite the overall muddy mix.
